[Section: Love is the root of every action]

Since love is the root of every action, whether true or false, the root of religious actions is love of Allah and His Messenger, just as the root of religious statements is affirmation (taṣdīq) of Allah and His Messenger. Every desire that prevents the perfection of love for Allah and His Messenger and competes with this love, or every doubt that prevents the perfection of affirmation, opposes the root of faith or weakens it. If it grows strong enough to oppose the root of love and affirmation, it becomes disbelief or major shirk (shirk akbar). If it does not oppose it, it nonetheless detracts from its perfection, leaving weakness and lethargy in resolve and seeking. Such desires veil the one who has arrived, cut off the one who seeks, and turn back the one who is eager. Thus allegiance (muwālāh) is not valid except through enmity (mu'ādāh), as Allah the Exalted said, concerning the leader of the ḥanīfs, the lovers, that he said to his people: ﴿Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers before you? Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds﴾.

Thus the allegiance and intimate friendship (khullah) of the Friend of Allah (Khalīl Allāh) was not valid except by realizing this enmity, for there is no allegiance except through disavowal (barā'ah) from every object of worship other than Allah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship besides Allah. We have rejected you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone"﴾ [al-Mumtaḥanah: 4].

And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And [mention] when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except He who created me, for indeed He will guide me." And he made it a word lasting among his descendants that they might return﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 26–28].

That is, He made this allegiance to Allah and disavowal from every object of worship other than Him a word lasting among his descendants, which the prophets and their followers inherit from one another, and it is the word: "There is no deity except Allah" (lā ilāha illā Allāh). It is the word that the leader of the ḥanīfs bequeathed to his followers until the Day of Resurrection.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 26, verse 89:**

The sound heart (al-qalb al-salim) is the one free from rancour and corruption. Its reality is the heart that has submitted entirely to God Most High alone, so it is purified from the corruption and rancour of polytheism (shirk), and from the corruption of sins and acts of disobedience. Indeed, it is the heart that stays upright in the sincerity of its love and the goodness of its dealings. This is the heart for which salvation from His punishment and success in His honour are guaranteed. From this same root the word Islam is derived, for it means surrender, submission to God Most High, and freedom from the impurities of polytheism. So the one who submits to his Lord and is sincere toward Him is like a servant who has submitted to his master, with no "partners quarrelling" over him. For this reason God, glory be to Him, set out these two examples: the Muslim who is sincere and devoted to his Lord, and the one who associates others with Him.

From the same root comes salam (advance-payment contract) for the salaf (the earlier contract). Its reality is the consideration that is paid in advance, because the one who owes it has guaranteed its delivery to his creditor. Then the contract itself was named salam, and its reality is what we have mentioned.

If it is said: "Does this not contradict their calling the one bitten by a snake 'sound' (salim)?"

It is said: This is not a contradiction to it, but rather a confirmation of what we have said. They called him sound because of what concerns him, seeks it, and hopes that his condition will become one of safety. Nothing is more important to him than safety, and he seeks nothing else more eagerly. So he was named "sound" for this reason. This is of the same kind as their naming a deadly desert a "place of success" (mafāzah), because nothing is more important to one who traverses it than his success (fawz), that is, his deliverance from it. So it was called mafāzah because one seeks success (fawz) in it. This is better than their saying that it was called mafāzah and the bitten one was called "sound" only as an optimistic omen (tafā'ul). Although optimism is part of this meaning and is included in it, the meaning we have mentioned is more general and better.

He said in *al-Jawab al-Kafi*:

The sound heart is the one that is safe from polytheism, rancour, spite, envy, miserliness, arrogance, and love of the world and of leadership. It is safe from every affliction that distances it from God, safe from every doubt that opposes His report, and from every desire that opposes His command. It is safe from every will that competes with His will, and safe from every obstacle that cuts it off from God. This sound heart is in a paradise hastened in this world, in a paradise in the barzakh (intermediate state), and in the paradise of the Day of Return.

He said in *Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah*:

The sound heart, which is saved from God's punishment, is the heart that is safe from this and that. It is the heart that has submitted to its Lord and surrendered to His command, with no remaining dispute against His command and no opposition to His report. It is sound from everything other than God and His command. It desires only God and does nothing except what God has commanded. God alone is its ultimate goal, while His command and His law are its means and its path. No doubt can stand between it and the belief in His report, though doubts may pass by it, knowing that they have no abode in it. No desire can stand between it and following His good pleasure. When the heart is like this, it is sound from polytheism, sound from innovation (bid'ah), sound from error, and sound from falsehood. All the sayings that have been said about its interpretation are included in this.

Its reality is that it is the heart that has submitted to the servitude of its Lord out of modesty, fear, hope, and expectation. It has annihilated its love for anything other than Him through its love for Him, its fear of anything other than Him through its fear of Him, and its hope in anything other than Him through its hope in Him. It has submitted to His command and to His Messenger in belief and obedience, as has been mentioned. It has submitted to His decree and predestination, so it does not accuse Him or dispute with Him, and it does not resent His decrees. It submits to its Lord in compliance, humility, abasement, and servitude. It submits all its states, words, deeds, spiritual experiences, and inner perceptions, outwardly and inwardly, to the example of His Messenger (ﷺ), and it presents whatever comes from other than him to that example. What agrees with it is accepted, and what contradicts it is rejected. What does not clearly agree or disagree is held in suspension until its status becomes clear. It is at peace with His friends and His party, the successful ones who defend His religion and the Sunnah of His Prophet and uphold them, and it is hostile to His enemies, those who oppose His Book and the Sunnah of His Prophet, who depart from them and call to what contradicts them.

**(Benefit)**

The soundness of the heart is not complete in an absolute sense until it is safe from five things: polytheism, which contradicts monotheism (tawhid); innovation (bid'ah), which opposes the Sunnah; desire, which opposes the command; heedlessness, which contradicts remembrance; and whim, which contradicts sincere devotion and sincerity (ikhlas).

These five are veils between the servant and God, and under each of them are many kinds that contain countless particulars.

**(Section)**

The word salim means "safe," and it follows this pattern because it denotes attributes, like tawil ("long"), qasir ("short"), and zarif ("elegant"). So salim is the heart in which safety has become a fixed attribute, like ʿalim ("knowing") and qadir ("powerful"). It is also the opposite of "sick," and salim is the opposite of ʿalil (the one who is ill).

People's expressions about the meaning of the sound heart have varied.

The comprehensive matter that gathers all of this is that it is the heart that is safe from every desire that opposes God's command and prohibition, and from every doubt that opposes His report. It is safe from servitude to anything other than Him, and safe from ruling by anyone other than His Messenger. It is sound in its love, while it rules by His Messenger in its fear, its hope, its reliance upon Him, its turning to Him, its humility before Him, its preference for His pleasure in every state, and its distancing from His anger by every means. This is the reality of the servitude that is fit for God alone.

So the sound heart is the one that is free from having any partner with God in it in any way. Its servitude is purely for God, the Exalted: in will, love, trust, turning, humility, fear, and hope. Its deeds and commands are entirely for God. If it loves, it loves for God's sake; if it hates, it hates for God's sake; if it gives, it gives for God; if it withholds, it withholds for God. This is not enough for it unless it is also free from submission to and ruling by anyone other than the Messenger of God (ﷺ). It binds its heart to him with a firm bond of following and taking him alone as the model, above anyone else, in matters of wealth and deeds, including the actions of the heart, which are beliefs; the utterances of the tongue, which are reports of what is in the heart; the deeds of the heart, which are will, love, dislike, and their consequences; and the deeds of the limbs. So the judgement on all of this is in its exactness and its totality according to what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought. It does not advance ahead of him in belief, speech, or action, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger﴾ (Qur'an 49:1). That is: do not speak until he speaks, and do not act until he commands.

One of the earlier scholars (salaf) said: "No deed, however small, is done without two registers being opened for it": "Why?" and "How?" That is: why did you do it, and how did you do it?

The first is a question about the cause of the act, what moved and prompted it. Was it a hasty share of the doer's worldly portions, an aim of the self in loving praise from people and fearing their blame; or was it to attract an immediate beloved thing or repel an immediate hated thing? Or was the motive to fulfil the right of servitude to God, to seek closeness and affection with the Lord, glory be to Him, and to seek a means to Him?

The point of this question is: Was it incumbent upon you to do this deed for your Master, or did you do it for your own share and desire?

The second is your being asked about following the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, in that worship. That is: was that deed in accordance with what I prescribed for you through My messenger, or was it a deed I did not prescribe and did not approve?

The first is a question about sincerity (ikhlas), and the second is about following (mutaba'ah). God, glory be to Him, accepts no deed unless both are present.

The way to be freed from the first question is by purifying sincerity (tajrid al-ikhlas).

The way to be freed from the second question is by realising following.

The soundness of the heart is to be free from a will that contradicts sincerity, and from a desire that contradicts following. This is the reality of the soundness of the heart.

So whoever has a sound heart is guaranteed salvation and happiness.

**[Section: The difference between the soundness of the heart and simplicity and heedlessness]**

The difference between the soundness of the heart and simplicity (bulah) and heedlessness (ghafl) is that the soundness of the heart comes from not wanting evil after knowing it. Thus the heart is safe from wanting and intending it, not from ignorance of it. Simplicity and heedlessness, by contrast, are ignorance and lack of knowledge.

Such simplicity is not praiseworthy, because it is a deficiency. People only praise those who are like this for their being safe from evil. Perfection is for the heart to know the details of evil and yet be sound from wanting it. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I am not a cunning person, and cunning does not deceive me." ʿUmar was too intelligent to be deceived and too resolute to be fooled. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿The day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, except one who comes to God with a sound heart﴾ (Qur'an 26:88–89).

This is the one who is sound from the afflictions that afflict diseased hearts: the disease of doubt that makes one follow conjecture, and the disease of desire that makes one follow what the souls crave. So the sound heart is the one that is safe from this and from that.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 26, verses 96–98 (Part 1 of 2):

It is well known that they did not make their gods equal to Him, glorified is He, in creating, providing sustenance, causing death and life, dominion, or power. They only made them equal to Him in love, in worship (ta'alluh), and in submission and humbling themselves before them. This is the utmost ignorance and wrongdoing. How can dust be equated with the Lord of lords? How can slaves be equated with the Owner of necks? How can the poor in essence, the weak in essence, the incapable in essence, and the needy in essence, who has of himself nothing but non-existence, be equated with the self-sufficient in essence, the powerful in essence, whose self-sufficiency, power, dominion, existence, benevolence, knowledge, mercy, and perfect, absolute completeness are necessary attributes of His essence?

What injustice is more hideous than this? And what judgment is more oppressive than this? By it they equated the One who has no equal with His creation, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light. Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord.﴾ [al-An'am: 1].

So the polytheist equated the One who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light with one who does not possess for himself or for others an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth. What an "equality" that contains the greatest and most hideous injustice!

(Section)

This equating was only in love, in deifying, and in following what they legislated, not in creation, power, or lordship. That is the "equality" (adl) which He reported about the disbelievers, as in His saying:
6:1 All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord.

The more sound of the two opinions is that the meaning is: "Then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord," meaning they make for Him equals whom they love, revere, and worship, just as they worship Allah and exalt His command.

He said in Tariq al-Hijratayn:
This equating was not on their part in actions and attributes, such that they believed those (deities) to be equal to Allah, glorified is He, in His actions and attributes. Rather, it was an equating on their part between Allah and them in love, worship, and exaltation, while acknowledging the difference between Allah and them. Correcting this is the correcting of the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

It is therefore fitting for whoever advises his own soul and loves its happiness and salvation to be alert to this matter in knowledge and in action, and to make it the most important of things to him, the most exalted of his knowledge and deeds, for the whole affair rests upon it, all matters revolve around it, and the questioning on the Day of Resurrection is about it. Allah, exalted is He, said: {15:92–93} ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do.﴾ Several of the Salaf said: it concerns the statement "There is no god but Allah," and this is true. For the whole questioning is about it, about its rulings, its rights, its obligations, and its requirements. No one is ever questioned except about it and about its obligations, requirements, and rights. Abu al-'Aliyah said: "There are two statements about which the first and the last will be questioned: 'What did you used to worship?' and 'What did you answer the messengers?'"

So the question "What did you used to worship?" is the question about this statement itself. And the question "What did you answer the messengers?" is a question about the means and the path leading to it: did they follow it and respond to the messengers when they called them to it? Thus the whole matter returns to it. A matter of this nature deserves that one clasp it with the fingers, bite upon it with the molars, and grasp it as one grasps hot coals.

It is not to be taken with the fingertips, nor sought as a leftover; rather, it should be made the greatest aim, and everything else should be sought only as a surplus. Allah is the Granter of success; there is no god but Him, and there is no lord other than Him.

[Section: Shirk is of two kinds: greater and lesser]

As for shirk, it is of two kinds: greater and lesser. The greater shirk is not forgiven by Allah except through repentance from it. It is taking a rival (nidd) besides Allah, loving it as one loves Allah. This is the shirk that involved equating the gods of the polytheists with the Lord of the worlds. For this reason they said to their gods in the Fire: ﴿By Allah, we were certainly in manifest error, when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 97–98], while acknowledging that Allah alone is the Creator of everything, its Lord and Sovereign, and that their gods do not create, are not provided for, do not give life, and do not cause death. This equating was only in love, exaltation, and worship, as is the condition of most polytheists in the world. Indeed, all of them love what they worship, exalt it, and befriend it besides Allah. Many of them, indeed most of them, love their gods more than they love Allah; they rejoice at the mention of their gods more than they rejoice when Allah alone is mentioned; and they become angrier at one who disparages their deities and gods, from among the shaykhs, than they become when someone disparages the Lord of the worlds. When a sacred thing of their gods and objects of worship is violated, they become angry like a lion when it is provoked; but when the sacred things of Allah are violated, they do not get angry for them. Rather, if the violator of them feeds them something, they are pleased with him, and their hearts do not object to him. We have witnessed this ourselves, and others among them have witnessed it openly. You see one of them making the mention of his deity and object of worship besides Allah a constant habit on his tongue, whether he is standing or sitting, whether he stumbles, falls ill, or feels lonely. The mention of his deity and object of worship besides Allah is what dominates his heart and tongue, and he does not deny this; he claims it is the gate of his need toward Allah, his intercessor with Him, and his means to Him.

Thus it was with the worshippers of idols alike. This is the quantity that stood in their hearts, and the polytheists inherited it according to the variation of their gods: those (earlier ones) had gods made of stone, and others took gods from humans. Allah, exalted is He, said, relating about the predecessors of these polytheists: ﴿And those who take protectors besides Him say, "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position." Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ.﴾ [al-Zumar: 3].

Then He testified against them of disbelief and lying, and reported that He does not guide them, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar and a disbeliever.﴾

This is the condition of one who takes a protector besides Allah, claiming that it brings him closer to Allah. How rare is one who is freed from this! Indeed, how rare is one who does not oppose the one who denies it!

What is in the hearts of these polytheists and their predecessors is that their gods intercede for them with Allah. This is the very essence of shirk. Allah denounced this in His Book and nullified it, and He reported that all intercession belongs to Him, and that no one intercedes with Him except for one whom Allah permits to intercede for, and whose statement and action He is pleased with. These are the people of monotheism (tawhid), who did not take intercessors besides Allah. He, glorified is He, permits whomever He wills to intercede for them, since they did not take intercessors besides Him. So the happiest of people through the intercession of the one whom Allah permits is the possessor of monotheism who did not take an intercessor besides Allah, his Lord and his Master.

The intercession that Allah and His Messenger affirmed is the intercession that proceeds from His permission for the one who professes His oneness. The intercession that Allah negated is the shirk-based intercession that exists in the hearts of the polytheists, who take intercessors besides Allah. Such people are treated in the opposite of their intention regarding their intercessors, while the monotheists are the ones who attain it.

Reflect on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to Abu Hurayrah, when he asked him: "Who will be the happiest of people with your intercession, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The happiest of people with my intercession is the one who says, 'There is no god but Allah,' sincerely from his heart." Observe how he made the greatest cause by which his intercession is attained the purification of monotheism. This is the opposite of what the polytheists believe: that intercession is attained by taking their friends as intercessors and worshipping and befriending them besides Allah. So the Prophet (ﷺ) reversed their false claim and reported that the cause of intercession is the purification of monotheism; then Allah permits the intercessor to intercede.

Among the ignorance of the polytheist is his belief that whoever he takes as a protector or intercessor will intercede for him and benefit him with Allah, just as the intercessions of the close companions of kings and rulers benefit those who are loyal to them. They do not know that no one intercedes with Him except by His permission, and that He does not permit intercession except for one whose statement and action He is pleased with, as Allah, exalted is He, said in the first section: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255].

In the second section: ﴿And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 28]. There remains a third section, which is that He is not pleased with any statement or action except monotheism and following the Messenger. It is about these two statements that the first and the last will be questioned, as Abu al-'Aliyah said: "There are two statements about which the first and the last will be questioned: 'What did you used to worship?' and 'What did you answer the messengers?'"

These are three principles that cut the tree of shirk from the heart of whoever comprehends and understands them: there is no intercession except by His permission; He permits none except one whose statement and action He approves; and He is not pleased with any statement or action except His monotheism and following His Messenger. Allah, exalted is He, does not forgive the shirk of those who equate others with Him, as He said: ﴿Then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord.﴾ [al-An'am: 1]. The more sound of the two opinions is that they equate others with Him in worship, befriending, and love, as in the other verse: ﴿By Allah, we were certainly in manifest error, when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 97–98], and as in the verse of al-Baqarah: ﴿And among the people are those who take other than Allah as equals, loving them as they love Allah.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 165].

You see the polytheist contradicting his state and action with his speech. He says, "We do not love them as we love Allah, nor do we equate them with Allah." Yet he becomes angrier for them and their sacred things when they are violated than he becomes for Allah, rejoices at their mention, is delighted by it, especially when it is said of them what is not in them, such as relieving distress, removing hardships, fulfilling needs, and that they are the gateway between Allah and His servants. You see the polytheist rejoicing, becoming happy, and his heart longing; there stirs in him the fervent passion of exaltation, submission to them, and loyalty. But when you mention Allah alone to him, and single out His monotheism, he is seized by loneliness, constriction, and distress, he accuses you of deficiency in the divinity that is theirs, and perhaps he becomes hostile to you.

By Allah, we have seen this from them directly. They have shot us with their enmity, plotted against us, and Allah will disgrace them in this world and the Hereafter. Their argument was nothing but what their brethren said: "He has reviled our gods." So these said: "You have disparaged our shaykhs and the gates of our needs to Allah." Likewise the Christians said to the Prophet (ﷺ), when he said to them: "Indeed, the Messiah is a servant of Allah," they said: "You have disparaged and reviled the Messiah." Likewise the likes of the polytheists said to whoever forbade taking graves as idols to be worshipped and mosques to be visited, and who commanded visiting them in the manner that Allah and His Messenger permitted: "You have disparaged their people."

Look at this resemblance between their hearts, as though they had mutually bequeathed it: ﴿Whomever Allah guides is the one rightly guided, but whomever He leaves astray, you will never find for him a protector to guide him.﴾ [al-Kahf: 17].

Allah, exalted is He, has cut off all the means on which the polytheists relied, entirely, with a cutting that whoever contemplates and recognizes it knows: whoever takes a protector or intercessor besides Allah is like the spider that takes a house, and indeed the weakest of houses is the spider's house. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: "Call upon those you claimed besides Allah. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, nor do they have therein any share, nor is there for Him any helper among them." And intercession with Him does not benefit except for one whom He has permitted.﴾ [Saba': 22–23].

The polytheist takes his object of worship only because he believes he will gain benefit from it, and benefit comes only from one who has one of these four qualities: either he owns what his servants seek from Him; if not, then he is a partner of the Owner; if not a partner, then he is a helper and supporter to Him; and if not a helper or supporter, then he is an intercessor with Him.

So He, glorified is He, negated the four ranks in a sequenced negation, descending from the highest to what is below it. He negated ownership, partnership, support, and the intercession that the polytheist imagines, and He affirmed an intercession in which no polytheist has any share: intercession by His permission.

But the matter is as ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The bonds of Islam are undone only strand by strand, when there grows up in Islam one who does not know the jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam)."

This is because whoever does not know the jahiliyyah and the shirk (associating partners with Allah), and what the Qur'an reproached and condemned, will fall into it and approve of it. He will call to it, declare it correct, and beautify it, while not knowing that it is what the people of the jahiliyyah were upon, or its like, or worse than it, or lesser than it. Whoever has insight and a living heart sees this plainly, and Allah is the One sought for help.

Also like a man saying to another: "What Allah wills and you will," "This is from Allah and from you," "We are by Allah and by you," "I have none but Allah and you," "I put my trust in Allah and in you," and "Were it not for you, such and such would not have happened." This may be the greater shirk, depending on the speaker and his intention. It is also established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said to a man who said to him, "What Allah wills and what you will": "Have you made me a rival (nidd) to Allah? Say: What Allah alone wills." And this wording is lighter than other expressions.

What is astonishing is that they say: "This is not prostration; it is merely placing the head before the shaykh out of respect and humility." Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 26, verses 96–98 (Part 1 of 2):

It is well known that they did not make their gods equal to Him, glorified is He, in creating, providing sustenance, causing death and life, dominion, or power. They only made them equal to Him in love, in worship (ta'alluh), and in submission and humbling themselves before them. This is the utmost ignorance and wrongdoing. How can dust be equated with the Lord of lords? How can slaves be equated with the Owner of necks? How can the poor in essence, the weak in essence, the incapable in essence, and the needy in essence, who has of himself nothing but non-existence, be equated with the self-sufficient in essence, the powerful in essence, whose self-sufficiency, power, dominion, existence, benevolence, knowledge, mercy, and perfect, absolute completeness are necessary attributes of His essence?

What injustice is more hideous than this? And what judgment is more oppressive than this? By it they equated the One who has no equal with His creation, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light. Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord.﴾ [al-An'am: 1].

So the polytheist equated the One who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light with one who does not possess for himself or for others an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth. What an "equality" that contains the greatest and most hideous injustice!

(Section)

This equating was only in love, in deifying, and in following what they legislated, not in creation, power, or lordship. That is the "equality" (adl) which He reported about the disbelievers, as in His saying:
6:1 All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord.

The more sound of the two opinions is that the meaning is: "Then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord," meaning they make for Him equals whom they love, revere, and worship, just as they worship Allah and exalt His command.

He said in Tariq al-Hijratayn:
This equating was not on their part in actions and attributes, such that they believed those (deities) to be equal to Allah, glorified is He, in His actions and attributes. Rather, it was an equating on their part between Allah and them in love, worship, and exaltation, while acknowledging the difference between Allah and them. Correcting this is the correcting of the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

It is therefore fitting for whoever advises his own soul and loves its happiness and salvation to be alert to this matter in knowledge and in action, and to make it the most important of things to him, the most exalted of his knowledge and deeds, for the whole affair rests upon it, all matters revolve around it, and the questioning on the Day of Resurrection is about it. Allah, exalted is He, said: {15:92–93} ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do.﴾ Several of the Salaf said: it concerns the statement "There is no god but Allah," and this is true. For the whole questioning is about it, about its rulings, its rights, its obligations, and its requirements. No one is ever questioned except about it and about its obligations, requirements, and rights. Abu al-'Aliyah said: "There are two statements about which the first and the last will be questioned: 'What did you used to worship?' and 'What did you answer the messengers?'"

So the question "What did you used to worship?" is the question about this statement itself. And the question "What did you answer the messengers?" is a question about the means and the path leading to it: did they follow it and respond to the messengers when they called them to it? Thus the whole matter returns to it. A matter of this nature deserves that one clasp it with the fingers, bite upon it with the molars, and grasp it as one grasps hot coals.

It is not to be taken with the fingertips, nor sought as a leftover; rather, it should be made the greatest aim, and everything else should be sought only as a surplus. Allah is the Granter of success; there is no god but Him, and there is no lord other than Him.

[Section: Shirk is of two kinds: greater and lesser]

It is taking a rival (nidd) besides Allah, loving it as one loves Allah. This is the shirk that involved equating the gods of the polytheists with the Lord of the worlds. For this reason they said to their gods in the Fire: ﴿By Allah, we were certainly in manifest error, when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 97–98], while acknowledging that Allah alone is the Creator of everything, its Lord and Sovereign, and that their gods do not create, are not provided for, do not give life, and do not cause death. This equating was only in love, exaltation, and worship, as is the condition of most polytheists in the world. Indeed, all of them love what they worship, exalt it, and befriend it besides Allah. Many of them, indeed most of them, love their gods more than they love Allah; they rejoice at the mention of their gods more than they rejoice when Allah alone is mentioned; and they become angrier at one who disparages their deities and gods, from among the shaykhs, than they become when someone disparages the Lord of the worlds. When a sacred thing of their gods and objects of worship is violated, they become angry like a lion when it is provoked; but when the sacred things of Allah are violated, they do not get angry for them. Rather, if the violator of them feeds them something, they are pleased with him, and their hearts do not object to him. We have witnessed this ourselves, and others among them have witnessed it openly. You see one of them making the mention of his deity and object of worship besides Allah a constant habit on his tongue, whether he is standing or sitting, whether he stumbles, falls ill, or feels lonely. The mention of his deity and object of worship besides Allah is what dominates his heart and tongue, and he does not deny this; he claims it is the gate of his need toward Allah, his intercessor with Him, and his means to Him.

Thus it was with the worshippers of idols alike. This is the quantity that stood in their hearts, and the polytheists inherited it according to the variation of their gods: those (earlier ones) had gods made of stone, and others took gods from humans. Allah, exalted is He, said, relating about the predecessors of these polytheists: ﴿And those who take protectors besides Him say, "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position." Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ.﴾ [al-Zumar: 3].

Then He testified against them of disbelief and lying, and reported that He does not guide them, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar and a disbeliever.﴾

This is the condition of one who takes a protector besides Allah, claiming that it brings him closer to Allah. How rare is one who is freed from this! Indeed, how rare is one who does not oppose the one who denies it!

What is in the hearts of these polytheists and their predecessors is that their gods intercede for them with Allah. This is the very essence of shirk. Allah denounced this in His Book and nullified it, and He reported that all intercession belongs to Him, and that no one intercedes with Him except for one whom Allah permits to intercede for, and whose statement and action He is pleased with. These are the people of monotheism (tawhid), who did not take intercessors besides Allah. He, glorified is He, permits whomever He wills to intercede for them, since they did not take intercessors besides Him. So the happiest of people through the intercession of the one whom Allah permits is the possessor of monotheism who did not take an intercessor besides Allah, his Lord and his Master.

The intercession that Allah and His Messenger affirmed is the intercession that proceeds from His permission for the one who professes His oneness. The intercession that Allah negated is the shirk-based intercession that exists in the hearts of the polytheists, who take intercessors besides Allah. Such people are treated in the opposite of their intention regarding their intercessors, while the monotheists are the ones who attain it.

Reflect on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to Abu Hurayrah, when he asked him: "Who will be the happiest of people with your intercession, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The happiest of people with my intercession is the one who says, 'There is no god but Allah,' sincerely from his heart." Observe how he made the greatest cause by which his intercession is attained the purification of monotheism. This is the opposite of what the polytheists believe: that intercession is attained by taking their friends as intercessors and worshipping and befriending them besides Allah. So the Prophet (ﷺ) reversed their false claim and reported that the cause of intercession is the purification of monotheism; then Allah permits the intercessor to intercede.

Among the ignorance of the polytheist is his belief that whoever he takes as a protector or intercessor will intercede for him and benefit him with Allah, just as the intercessions of the close companions of kings and rulers benefit those who are loyal to them. They do not know that no one intercedes with Him except by His permission, and that He does not permit intercession except for one whose statement and action He is pleased with, as Allah, exalted is He, said in the first section: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255].

In the second section: ﴿And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 28]. There remains a third section, which is that He is not pleased with any statement or action except monotheism and following the Messenger. Yet he becomes angrier for them and their sacred things when they are violated than he becomes for Allah, rejoices at their mention, is delighted by it, especially when it is said of them what is not in them, such as relieving distress, removing hardships, fulfilling needs, and that they are the gateway between Allah and His servants. You see the polytheist rejoicing, becoming happy, and his heart longing; there stirs in him the fervent passion of exaltation, submission to them, and loyalty. For if a servant is saved from it, and from ta'til (denial of Allah's attributes), which are the two diseases by which nations were destroyed, then whatever comes after them is easier than them. And if he is destroyed by them, then he goes the way of those who were destroyed, and I do not grieve over the destroyed.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 26, verses 96–98 (Part 1 of 2):

It is well known that they did not make their gods equal to Him, glorified is He, in creating, providing sustenance, causing death and life, dominion, or power. They only made them equal to Him in love, in worship (ta'alluh), and in submission and humbling themselves before them. This is the utmost ignorance and wrongdoing. How can dust be equated with the Lord of lords? How can slaves be equated with the Owner of necks? How can the poor in essence, the weak in essence, the incapable in essence, and the needy in essence, who has of himself nothing but non-existence, be equated with the self-sufficient in essence, the powerful in essence, whose self-sufficiency, power, dominion, existence, benevolence, knowledge, mercy, and perfect, absolute completeness are necessary attributes of His essence?

What injustice is more hideous than this? And what judgment is more oppressive than this? By it they equated the One who has no equal with His creation, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light. Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord.﴾ [al-An'am: 1].

So the polytheist equated the One who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light with one who does not possess for himself or for others an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth. What an "equality" that contains the greatest and most hideous injustice!

(Section)

This equating was only in love, in deifying, and in following what they legislated, not in creation, power, or lordship. That is the "equality" (adl) which He reported about the disbelievers, as in His saying:
6:1 All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord.

The more sound of the two opinions is that the meaning is: "Then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord," meaning they make for Him equals whom they love, revere, and worship, just as they worship Allah and exalt His command.

He said in Tariq al-Hijratayn:
This equating was not on their part in actions and attributes, such that they believed those (deities) to be equal to Allah, glorified is He, in His actions and attributes. Rather, it was an equating on their part between Allah and them in love, worship, and exaltation, while acknowledging the difference between Allah and them. Correcting this is the correcting of the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

It is therefore fitting for whoever advises his own soul and loves its happiness and salvation to be alert to this matter in knowledge and in action, and to make it the most important of things to him, the most exalted of his knowledge and deeds, for the whole affair rests upon it, all matters revolve around it, and the questioning on the Day of Resurrection is about it. Allah, exalted is He, said: {15:92–93} ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do.﴾ Several of the Salaf said: it concerns the statement "There is no god but Allah," and this is true. For the whole questioning is about it, about its rulings, its rights, its obligations, and its requirements. No one is ever questioned except about it and about its obligations, requirements, and rights. Abu al-'Aliyah said: "There are two statements about which the first and the last will be questioned: 'What did you used to worship?' and 'What did you answer the messengers?'"

So the question "What did you used to worship?" is the question about this statement itself. And the question "What did you answer the messengers?" is a question about the means and the path leading to it: did they follow it and respond to the messengers when they called them to it? Thus the whole matter returns to it. A matter of this nature deserves that one clasp it with the fingers, bite upon it with the molars, and grasp it as one grasps hot coals.

It is not to be taken with the fingertips, nor sought as a leftover; rather, it should be made the greatest aim, and everything else should be sought only as a surplus. Allah is the Granter of success; there is no god but Him, and there is no lord other than Him.

[Section: Shirk is of two kinds: greater and lesser]

As for shirk, it is of two kinds: greater and lesser. The greater shirk is not forgiven by Allah except through repentance from it. It is taking a rival (nidd) besides Allah, loving it as one loves Allah. This is the shirk that involved equating the gods of the polytheists with the Lord of the worlds. For this reason they said to their gods in the Fire: ﴿By Allah, we were certainly in manifest error, when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 97–98], while acknowledging that Allah alone is the Creator of everything, its Lord and Sovereign, and that their gods do not create, are not provided for, do not give life, and do not cause death. This equating was only in love, exaltation, and worship, as is the condition of most polytheists in the world. Indeed, all of them love what they worship, exalt it, and befriend it besides Allah. Many of them, indeed most of them, love their gods more than they love Allah; they rejoice at the mention of their gods more than they rejoice when Allah alone is mentioned; and they become angrier at one who disparages their deities and gods, from among the shaykhs, than they become when someone disparages the Lord of the worlds. When a sacred thing of their gods and objects of worship is violated, they become angry like a lion when it is provoked; but when the sacred things of Allah are violated, they do not get angry for them. Rather, if the violator of them feeds them something, they are pleased with him, and their hearts do not object to him. We have witnessed this ourselves, and others among them have witnessed it openly. You see one of them making the mention of his deity and object of worship besides Allah a constant habit on his tongue, whether he is standing or sitting, whether he stumbles, falls ill, or feels lonely. The mention of his deity and object of worship besides Allah is what dominates his heart and tongue, and he does not deny this; he claims it is the gate of his need toward Allah, his intercessor with Him, and his means to Him.

Thus it was with the worshippers of idols alike. This is the quantity that stood in their hearts, and the polytheists inherited it according to the variation of their gods: those (earlier ones) had gods made of stone, and others took gods from humans. Allah, exalted is He, said, relating about the predecessors of these polytheists: ﴿And those who take protectors besides Him say, "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position." Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ.﴾ [al-Zumar: 3].

Then He testified against them of disbelief and lying, and reported that He does not guide them, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar and a disbeliever.﴾

This is the condition of one who takes a protector besides Allah, claiming that it brings him closer to Allah. How rare is one who is freed from this! Indeed, how rare is one who does not oppose the one who denies it!

What is in the hearts of these polytheists and their predecessors is that their gods intercede for them with Allah. This is the very essence of shirk. Allah denounced this in His Book and nullified it, and He reported that all intercession belongs to Him, and that no one intercedes with Him except for one whom Allah permits to intercede for, and whose statement and action He is pleased with. These are the people of monotheism (tawhid), who did not take intercessors besides Allah. He, glorified is He, permits whomever He wills to intercede for them, since they did not take intercessors besides Him. So the happiest of people through the intercession of the one whom Allah permits is the possessor of monotheism who did not take an intercessor besides Allah, his Lord and his Master.

The intercession that Allah and His Messenger affirmed is the intercession that proceeds from His permission for the one who professes His oneness. The intercession that Allah negated is the shirk-based intercession that exists in the hearts of the polytheists, who take intercessors besides Allah. Such people are treated in the opposite of their intention regarding their intercessors, while the monotheists are the ones who attain it.

Reflect on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to Abu Hurayrah, when he asked him: "Who will be the happiest of people with your intercession, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The happiest of people with my intercession is the one who says, 'There is no god but Allah,' sincerely from his heart." Observe how he made the greatest cause by which his intercession is attained the purification of monotheism. This is the opposite of what the polytheists believe: that intercession is attained by taking their friends as intercessors and worshipping and befriending them besides Allah. So the Prophet (ﷺ) reversed their false claim and reported that the cause of intercession is the purification of monotheism; then Allah permits the intercessor to intercede.

Among the ignorance of the polytheist is his belief that whoever he takes as a protector or intercessor will intercede for him and benefit him with Allah, just as the intercessions of the close companions of kings and rulers benefit those who are loyal to them. They do not know that no one intercedes with Him except by His permission, and that He does not permit intercession except for one whose statement and action He is pleased with, as Allah, exalted is He, said in the first section: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255].

In the second section: ﴿And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 28]. There remains a third section, which is that He is not pleased with any statement or action except monotheism and following the Messenger. It is about these two statements that the first and the last will be questioned, as Abu al-'Aliyah said: "There are two statements about which the first and the last will be questioned: 'What did you used to worship?' and 'What did you answer the messengers?'"

These are three principles that cut the tree of shirk from the heart of whoever comprehends and understands them: there is no intercession except by His permission; He permits none except one whose statement and action He approves; and He is not pleased with any statement or action except His monotheism and following His Messenger. Allah, exalted is He, does not forgive the shirk of those who equate others with Him, as He said: ﴿Then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord.﴾ [al-An'am: 1]. The more sound of the two opinions is that they equate others with Him in worship, befriending, and love, as in the other verse: ﴿By Allah, we were certainly in manifest error, when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 97–98], and as in the verse of al-Baqarah: ﴿And among the people are those who take other than Allah as equals, loving them as they love Allah.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 165].

You see the polytheist contradicting his state and action with his speech. He says, "We do not love them as we love Allah, nor do we equate them with Allah." Yet he becomes angrier for them and their sacred things when they are violated than he becomes for Allah, rejoices at their mention, is delighted by it, especially when it is said of them what is not in them, such as relieving distress, removing hardships, fulfilling needs, and that they are the gateway between Allah and His servants. You see the polytheist rejoicing, becoming happy, and his heart longing; there stirs in him the fervent passion of exaltation, submission to them, and loyalty. But when you mention Allah alone to him, and single out His monotheism, he is seized by loneliness, constriction, and distress, he accuses you of deficiency in the divinity that is theirs, and perhaps he becomes hostile to you.

By Allah, we have seen this from them directly. They have shot us with their enmity, plotted against us, and Allah will disgrace them in this world and the Hereafter. Their argument was nothing but what their brethren said: "He has reviled our gods." So these said: "You have disparaged our shaykhs and the gates of our needs to Allah." Likewise the Christians said to the Prophet (ﷺ), when he said to them: "Indeed, the Messiah is a servant of Allah," they said: "You have disparaged and reviled the Messiah." Likewise the likes of the polytheists said to whoever forbade taking graves as idols to be worshipped and mosques to be visited, and who commanded visiting them in the manner that Allah and His Messenger permitted: "You have disparaged their people."

Look at this resemblance between their hearts, as though they had mutually bequeathed it: ﴿Whomever Allah guides is the one rightly guided, but whomever He leaves astray, you will never find for him a protector to guide him.﴾ [al-Kahf: 17].

Allah, exalted is He, has cut off all the means on which the polytheists relied, entirely, with a cutting that whoever contemplates and recognizes it knows: whoever takes a protector or intercessor besides Allah is like the spider that takes a house, and indeed the weakest of houses is the spider's house. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: "Call upon those you claimed besides Allah. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, nor do they have therein any share, nor is there for Him any helper among them." And intercession with Him does not benefit except for one whom He has permitted.﴾ [Saba': 22–23].

The polytheist takes his object of worship only because he believes he will gain benefit from it, and benefit comes only from one who has one of these four qualities: either he owns what his servants seek from Him; if not, then he is a partner of the Owner; if not a partner, then he is a helper and supporter to Him; and if not a helper or supporter, then he is an intercessor with Him.

So He, glorified is He, negated the four ranks in a sequenced negation, descending from the highest to what is below it. He negated ownership, partnership, support, and the intercession that the polytheist imagines, and He affirmed an intercession in which no polytheist has any share: intercession by His permission.

Thus this verse is sufficient as light, proof, salvation, and purification of monotheism, and a severing of the roots of shirk and its consequences for whoever comprehends it. The Qur'an is full of its likes and parallels, but most people do not perceive the entry of the reality under it and its inclusion of it, and they assume it refers to a type and a people who passed away before and left no heirs. This is what stands between the heart and understanding the Qur'an.

By the life of Allah, if those people have passed away, there has nevertheless inherited them someone who is like them, or worse than them, or lesser than them. The Qur'an's address to these later people is like its address to those earlier ones. But the matter is as ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The bonds of Islam are undone only strand by strand, when there grows up in Islam one who does not know the jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam)."

This is because whoever does not know the jahiliyyah and the shirk (associating partners with Allah), and what the Qur'an reproached and condemned, will fall into it and approve of it. He will call to it, declare it correct, and beautify it, while not knowing that it is what the people of the jahiliyyah were upon, or its like, or worse than it, or lesser than it. Thus he undoes the bonds of Islam from his heart. The known becomes the disapproved, the disapproved becomes the known, the innovation (bidʿah) becomes a sunnah (prophetic practice), and the sunnah becomes an innovation. A man may disbelieve through the mere presence of faith and the stripping away of tawhid (monotheism), and be branded an innovator through stripping away following the Messenger ﷺ and abandoning desires and innovations. Whoever has insight and a living heart sees this plainly, and Allah is the One sought for help.

**Section.** As for the lesser shirk (shirk asghar), it is like slight showing-off (riyaʾ), affectation before people, and swearing by other than Allah, as is established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever swears by other than Allah has committed shirk." Also like a man saying to another: "What Allah wills and you will," "This is from Allah and from you," "We are by Allah and by you," "I have none but Allah and you," "I put my trust in Allah and in you," and "Were it not for you, such and such would not have happened." This may be the greater shirk, depending on the speaker and his intention. It is also established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said to a man who said to him, "What Allah wills and what you will": "Have you made me a rival (nidd) to Allah? Say: What Allah alone wills." And this wording is lighter than other expressions.

Among the kinds of shirk is the prostration of a disciple (murid) to a shaykh. It is shirk on the part of the one who prostrates and the one prostrated to. What is astonishing is that they say: "This is not prostration; it is merely placing the head before the shaykh out of respect and humility." It is said to them: "Even if you name it other than what you name it, the reality of prostration is placing the head before the one to whom one prostrates. Likewise, prostration to an idol, to the sun, to a star, or to a stone is all placing the head before it."

Among its kinds is the bowing of those who wear turbans (muʿammimin) to one another upon meeting. This is prostration in linguistic usage, and it was the basis of the explanation of His saying, ﴿Enter the gate prostrating﴾ [al-Nisaʾ: 154], meaning bowing down. Otherwise, it is not possible to enter with the forehead on the ground. From this is the Arabs' saying: "The trees prostrated" when the wind bent them.

Among its kinds is shaving the head for a shaykh, for it is worship offered to other than Allah. Shaving the head is not performed as worship except in the rites of pilgrimage (nusuk) for Allah alone.

Among its kinds is repentance (tawbah) to a shaykh, for this is a great shirk, since repentance is only for Allah, like prayer, fasting, the Hajj, and the rites of pilgrimage. It is the pure right of Allah.

In al-Musnad: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought a captive, and he said: 'O Allah, I repent to You, and I do not repent to Muhammad.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'He recognized the truth for its people.'"

So repentance is an act of worship that is not fitting except for Allah, like prostration and fasting.

Among its kinds is vowing (nadhr) to other than Allah, for this is shirk. It is greater than swearing by other than Allah. If whoever swears by other than Allah has committed shirk, then how about whoever vows to other than Allah? Moreover, in the Sunan, from the hadith of ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir, from him ﷺ: "A vow is an oath."

Among its kinds: fearing other than Allah, relying upon other than Allah, working for other than Allah, turning in repentance and submission, humbling oneself to other than Allah, seeking provision from other than Allah, praising other than Him for what He gave, being content with that in place of praising Him, glorified be He, blaming and being angry at what He did not decree and what the divine decree did not bring about, attributing His blessings to other than Him, and believing that there could be in existence something He does not will.

Among its kinds is seeking needs from the dead, seeking help from them, and turning toward them.

This is the root of the shirk of the world. The dead person's deeds have ceased, and he owns no harm or benefit for himself, let alone for one who seeks his help and asks him to fulfill his need, or asks him to intercede for him with Allah regarding it. This comes from his ignorance of the intercessor and of the one for whom intercession is sought before Him, as previously mentioned. He cannot intercede with Allah except with His permission, and Allah has not made seeking his help and asking him a cause for permission. The cause of His permission is only the perfection of tawhid. This polytheist has brought a cause that prevents permission, and he is like one who seeks help in a need through something that prevents its fulfillment. This is the condition of every polytheist. The dead person needs someone to pray for him, to have mercy upon him, and to ask forgiveness for him, just as the Prophet ﷺ instructed us: when we visit the graves of the Muslims, we should ask mercy for them and seek well-being and forgiveness for them.

The polytheists reversed this. They visited graves as an act of worship, to seek the fulfillment of needs and to seek help from their occupants. They made their graves into idols worshipped, called going to them "Hajj," took standing (waqfah) and head-shaving there, and so combined shirk with the true Deity, altering His religion, opposing the people of tawhid, and attributing to the people of tawhid a disparagement of the dead. Yet they themselves disparaged the Creator through shirk, and disparaged His allies who monotheistically worship Him and associate nothing with Him, through blaming them, reproaching them, and opposing them. They disparaged to the utmost degree those they associated with Him, since they thought they were pleased with this from them, that they had commanded them to it, and that they were allied with them upon it. These are the enemies of the Messengers and of tawhid in every time and place. How many are those who respond to them! And Allah's close friend, Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when he says: ﴿And keep me and my sons far from worshipping idols. My Lord, they have led many people astray﴾ [Ibrahim: 35–36].

None is saved from the snare of this greatest shirk except one who has made his tawhid pure for Allah, opposed the polytheists for the sake of Allah, drawn near to Allah through their hatred, and taken Allah alone as his Guardian, his Deity, and his object of worship. He makes his love purely for Allah, his fear purely for Allah, his hope purely for Allah, his humility purely for Allah, his reliance purely upon Allah, his seeking help purely from Allah, his refuge purely with Allah, and his seeking aid purely from Allah. He makes his intention sincere for Allah, following His command and seeking His pleasure. When he asks, he asks Allah; when he seeks help, he seeks help from Allah; when he acts, he acts for Allah. He is for Allah, by Allah, and with Allah.

Shirk has many kinds that no one can enumerate except Allah.

If we were to mention its kinds, the discourse would expand enormously. Perhaps Allah will facilitate writing a book on it, its divisions, its causes and origins, its harm, and what repels it.

For if a servant is saved from it, and from ta'til (denial of Allah's attributes), which are the two diseases by which nations were destroyed, then whatever comes after them is easier than them. And if he is destroyed by them, then he goes the way of those who were destroyed, and I do not grieve over the destroyed.

He, glorified is He, mentions in Surah al-Shu'ara' the various kinds of punishment that He inflicted upon the polytheists, and He mentions His saving of the people of tawhid (monotheism). Then He says: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers. And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful﴾.

So He mentions the shirk (associating partners with Allah) of those who deserved destruction because of it, and the tawhid of those who deserved salvation because of it.

Then He informs that in that there is a sign and a proof for the believers.

Then He mentions the source of all of that, and that it comes from His names and attributes. The destruction comes from His might ('izzah), and that salvation comes from His mercy (rahmah).

(Chapter: On the Shortness of Hope)

As for shortness of hope (qisar al-amal): it is knowledge of the nearness of departure and the swiftness with which the term of life ends. It is among the most beneficial of things for the heart, for it moves the heart to seize the days and to take advantage of opportunities that pass by like clouds, and to hasten to fold up the pages of one's deeds. It stirs the dormant resolve of the heart toward the Abode of Permanence (dar al-baqa'), and urges it to prepare its provision for the journey and to make up for what has passed. It makes one renounce the world and desire the Hereafter. When the heart constantly contemplates the shortness of hope, there stands within it a witness from the witnesses of certainty (yaqin), which seeks the annihilation of the world, the swiftness of its ending, the scarcity of what remains of it, and that it has departed in retreat; nothing remains of it except a remnant like the dregs of a vessel which its owner drains. And that nothing remains of it except as much as remains of a day whose sun has reached the peaks of the mountains. It shows one the lastingness and permanence of the Hereafter, that it has come forward in approach, that its signs and indications have arrived, and that meeting it is like a traveler whose companion has set out to meet him: each of them walks toward the other, and they are about to meet swiftly.

Sufficient regarding shortness of hope is His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿Have you considered: if We let them enjoy for years, then there comes to them that which they were promised, what good will that which they were given to enjoy avail them?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 205–207]

And His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And the Day He gathers them, it will be as though they had not remained but an hour of the day, recognizing one another among themselves﴾ [Yunus: 45]

And His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿As if, on the day they see it, they had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46]

And His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿They will say, "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who count." He will say, "You remained but a little, if only you had known."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 113–114] And His saying: ﴿As if, on the day they see what they are promised, they had not remained but an hour of a day — a proclamation. Will any be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35] And His saying: ﴿They will confide among themselves, "You remained not but ten." We know best what they will say when their most exemplary in course says, "You remained not but a day."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 103–104]

The Prophet (ﷺ) once addressed his Companions while the sun was upon the peaks of the mountains, and said: "Of the world, what has passed of it is nothing compared to what remains, except as much as remains of this day of yours of what has passed of it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by some of his Companions who were repairing a small shelter (khuss) of theirs which had decayed. He said: "What is this?" They said: "A shelter of ours which has decayed, so we are repairing it." He said: "I do not see the matter except as more hasty than this."

The building of shortness of hope rests on two matters: certainty of the world's cessation and departure from it, and certainty of meeting the Hereafter, its lastingness and permanence. Then one weighs the two matters against each other and gives preference to the one that is better to be preferred.

(Chapter: On the Shortness of Hope)

As for shortness of hope (qisar al-amal): it is knowledge of the nearness of departure and the swiftness with which the term of life ends. It is among the most beneficial of things for the heart, for it moves the heart to seize the days and to take advantage of opportunities that pass by like clouds, and to hasten to fold up the pages of one's deeds. It stirs the dormant resolve of the heart toward the Abode of Permanence (dar al-baqa'), and urges it to prepare its provision for the journey and to make up for what has passed. It makes one renounce the world and desire the Hereafter. When the heart constantly contemplates the shortness of hope, there stands within it a witness from the witnesses of certainty (yaqin), which seeks the annihilation of the world, the swiftness of its ending, the scarcity of what remains of it, and that it has departed in retreat; nothing remains of it except a remnant like the dregs of a vessel which its owner drains. And that nothing remains of it except as much as remains of a day whose sun has reached the peaks of the mountains. It shows one the lastingness and permanence of the Hereafter, that it has come forward in approach, that its signs and indications have arrived, and that meeting it is like a traveler whose companion has set out to meet him: each of them walks toward the other, and they are about to meet swiftly.

[Section: On the order of the call and its stages]

The first stage: prophethood.

The second: warning his closest kinsfolk (ʿashīrah).

The third: warning his people (qawm).

The fourth: warning a people to whom no warner had come before him, namely the Arabs as a whole.

The fifth: warning all who have been reached by his call, of both jinn and mankind, until the end of time.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 26, verse 227:

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And those who have wronged will soon know what return they will be returned to﴾, and the consensus (ijma') that it (ay, "what") is in the accusative governed by ﴿will return﴾, not by ﴿will know﴾.

It was conceivable that it be in the accusative governed by ﴿will know﴾ as an interrogative, but that it be a relative (mawsul) with the clause as its relative clause (silah) and a returning pronoun (a'id) omitted. However, what prevented this is a principle we have established and a proof we have set up: that when a relative noun is intended to refer to a verbal noun (masdar) and is connected to a verb derived from that verbal noun, it is not permitted, because of the absence of the intended benefit of the relative clause, which is clarifying and specifying the relative noun.

And a verbal noun does not clarify the verb derived from its own root, since it is, as it were, identical to it in wording and meaning, except in the case of varied types, as has been mentioned earlier.

He said: "There is another reason, stronger than this, which is that (ay) does not mean 'alladhi' (the one who) unless it is annexed to a definite noun, so you say: 'I met ayyuhum in the house,' for it is impossible for it to mean 'alladhi' while it is indefinite, and 'alladhi' is never indefinite. This is a principle upon which the rule concerning (ay) is built."
